key_insight: EHRAdapt adapts frozen language models to EHR tuples by combining a semantic prior for each event code with a learned residual, which helps especially when clinical events are rare.
clinical_relevance: This could improve prediction and classification from sparse, long-tailed health records by preserving clinical meaning without flattening EHR structure into text.
method: Maps EHR tuples directly into a frozen LM embedding space instead of serializing records as text.
Uses learned modality embeddings and time-gap attention biases to represent structure and temporal spacing.
Represents each event code as semantic prior + low-rank evidence residual, trained while keeping the backbone frozen.
evidence_signal: Across continued pretraining on about 4 million patients' records and three frozen backbones, the full adapter outperformed ablations on held-out next-event prediction and downstream infectious-disease/syndromic classification.
watch_item: Performance gains are shown on retrospective benchmarks, so real-world deployment would still need prospective validation and careful handling of rare-code coverage and ontology quality.
paper_title: EHRAdapt: Adapting Pretrained Language Models to Electronic Health Records with Semantic Priors for Rare Clinical Events
